details:
Jezero EVA Planner is a mission-critical, offline-capable flight-deck application designed for astronauts conducting surface extravehicular activities (EVAs) at Jezero Crater and the Three Forks habitat. Crews plot waypoints over real orbital imagery and Perseverance rover traverse data while the system continuously calculates suit oxygen reserves, local solar daylight remaining, and terrain slope hazards. Once a route is validated, astronauts can launch a Google-Maps-style active navigation session, log geological samples hands-free via offline-resilient speech recognition, and project essential telemetry onto a simulated helmet visor heads-up display (HUD) backed by 3D terrain visualization.

Benefits & Intended Impact

On Mars, communication delays with Earth mean astronauts must operate autonomously without live mission-control handholding. By replacing cluttered desktop tools with a high-contrast, glove-friendly interface, the planner reduces cognitive load and eliminates dangerous navigation errors. Features like single-tap "Return to Base" routing—which instantly calculates the safest walking path back to the habitat from the astronaut's current active position—directly protect crew survivability and streamline scientific sample collection during time-critical surface walks.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Mapping & Visualization: Leaflet.js for interactive 2D mapping, custom HTML5 Canvas/SVG rendering for elevation profiles and visor mini-maps, and 3D terrain modeling.
  • Data & Offline Architecture: NASA Mars Trek HiRISE orthomosaics, Perseverance rover traverse telemetry, USGS geological layers, Service Workers, and local browser storage for 100% offline persistence.
  • Accessibility & Voice: Browser-native Web Speech API with automatic offline text fallback, paired with bundled IBM Plex fonts.

Creativity & Key Design Factors

  • Dual-Device Visor Transition: Rather than treating planning and field execution separately, we created a "Send to HUD" mode that strips away non-essential menus and projects only vital survival metrics (oxygen, next waypoint, and return path) onto a transparent visor overlay.
  • Human Factors & Ergonomics: We designed the entire interface around pressurized spacesuit limitations—enforcing permanent glove-friendly touch targets, removing tiny text or all-caps clutter, and anchoring every calculation to local Martian solar time so crews never get caught in the dark after sunset.
